findings.title: Fabricator contents are swapped between the two fabricator files
findings.description: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` now holds the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. Each file's name points to the wrong content. The `category` fabricators still load, but anyone looking for the `:category` fabricator in `category_fabricator.rb` won't find it, and the embeddable_host fabricator is filed under the category name.

findings.title: Host lookup lowercases the column but not the bound value
findings.description: `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` lowercases only the stored column. `uri.host` is not downcased, so a referer such as `http://EvilTrout.com/page` yields `host = 'EvilTrout.com'`, which never equals a lowercased column value. The lookup then returns no match and the embed is rejected. The bound value needs `host.downcase`.

findings.title: Migration indexes a query result that may be empty
findings.description: `execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id']` raises `NoMethodError` on `nil` when no `embed_category` row matches a category, because `[0]` is nil on an empty result. The next line's `uncategorized_category_id` lookup has the same unguarded `[0]['value']` pattern.

findings.title: Store test requests fruit 2 but the fixture always returns fruit 1
findings.description: The test now calls `store.find('fruit', 2)`, but the pretender route `/fruits/:id` still returns `fruits[0]` (apple, `color_ids: [1,2]`) for any id. The assertions on colors 1 and 2 pass only because the fixture ignores the id. The test looks like it covers banana (id 2, `color_ids: [3]`) but actually covers apple.

findings.title: Test describe block misspells "embeddable"
findings.description: The new block is named `'with an emeddable host'`, which is a misspelling of "embeddable".

findings.title: Test describe name refers to the removed method
findings.description: The block is named `"allows_embeddable_host"`, the name of the removed `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?`, but the examples exercise `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`.

findings.title: Fallback `|| []` is unreachable
findings.description: `hydrated` is the result of `Array.prototype.map`, which is always an array and never falsy, so `hydrated || []` never uses the fallback. Separately, `_lookupSubType` can return `undefined` for a missing id, which leaves `undefined` entries in the array.

findings.title: `self.pluralize` existence could not be verified
findings.description: The new `_ids` branch calls `self.pluralize(subType)`. I could not confirm from the diff that the store defines `pluralize`. If it does not, the branch throws on any `*_ids` key.

findings.title: `replace('_', '-')` only replaces the first underscore
findings.description: `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first occurrence. The current `ADMIN_MODELS` entries have at most one underscore, so this does not break today. A type with two underscores would fail the lookup. A `/_/g` regex would avoid this.

findings.title: Migration interpolates host values into SQL
findings.description: The `INSERT` builds its values with `'#{h}'` string interpolation. The values come from an existing site setting, so the risk is low, but a host containing a quote would break the statement. Parameterized inserts would avoid this.
